competitive_landscape: The Cozumel ferry channel is served by frequent diesel catamarans (Ultramar, Winjet); coastal transfers up and down the Riviera Maya are road-bound and congested. No premium or electric water option exists.

journeys.with_navier: A silent, zero-emission foiling crossing — a premium tier on the Riviera Maya's signature channel.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Anchored by the ~9.5nm Cozumel crossing plus short Riviera Maya coastal hops — all in Pioneer II range, all ideal for an all-electric premium layer over the diesel fleet.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required for the near-shore Riviera Maya network.

precedents.why_it_matters: Commercial proof of the N30 in premium tourism transfer — applicable to the Riviera Maya.

regulatory_note: Coastal operations sit near the Mesoamerican reef and protected coastal zones; zero-wake foiling suits the marine environment. Engagement via API Quintana Roo / SEMAR.
seasonality: Year-round resort demand, peak Dec–Apr; hurricane-season window Jun–Nov; winter 'nortes' chop the channel.

summary: Playa del Carmen is the Riviera Maya's central resort town and the mainland terminus of the high-volume Cozumel ferry. Its Quinta Avenida tourism economy and dense beach-resort corridor make it one of the Caribbean coast's busiest waterfronts.
tagline: The Riviera Maya's beating heart and the mainland gateway to Cozumel.
